subject: Strange issue with new Stan-based package

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Strange issue with new Stan-based package
parts:
Hey everyone,

I've finally started working on an actual package based on Stan.
It builds and seems fine.

However, when I use 'mcmc' as the method (as opposed to vb), I get the following error:
Warning: namespace ‘bDif’ is not available and has been replaced
by .GlobalEnv when processing object ‘’

The code in question can be found at https://github.com/stephensrmmartin/bDif/blob/master/R/bDif.R lines 54-69
I'm calling bDifFit on some data. When I call that function with method='vb', it works fine (the inferences are questionable, but it at least runs).
On the other hand, method='mcmc' calls sampling() on stanmodels$difSimplex3 (just like vb does), and it gives the above error. Any ideas why?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Strange issue with new Stan-based package
parts:
On Friday, November 25, 2016 at 3:08:24 AM UTC-5, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Thursday, November 24, 2016 at 11:28:16 PM UTC-5, Stephen Martin wrote:
Is there any update on what could be causing this? Would updating stan/rstan to the latest development version help? (I have a git hub release from 2 wks ago installed).

No, but I'll try to fix it before rstan 2.13.x goes onto CRAN.

This is an odd error, but you don't need to do parallel chains to trigger it. Simply doing

library(bDif)
saveRDS(bDif:::stanmodels$difSimplex3, file = "/tmp/bDif_object.rda")
q("no")

and then in a new R session

obj <- readRDS("/tmp/bDif_object.rda") # same warning

So, something about the way your stanmodels are being created causes R to look for something in the bDif namespace (which is not yet available). This does not happen with the stanmodels in other R packages, such as rstanarm:::stanmodels$polr.

Ben

Thanks so much for looking at this. It seems that you *have* to import Rcpp into the namespace. That's the only necessary change (So I cherry picked from your PR).

Apparently methods isn't required for imports, and I think recent R versions assume methods as part of base; maybe cran has a separate policy though.

I chose to depend (not import) on rstan so that the rstan package is attached upon loading bDif, so all the rstan plotting and summary functions are also available. messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Strange issue with new Stan-based package
parts:
On Saturday, November 26, 2016 at 1:05:58 PM UTC-5, Stephen Martin wrote:
Thanks so much for looking at this. It seems that you *have* to import Rcpp into the namespace. That's the only necessary change (So I cherry picked from your PR).

Apparently methods isn't required for imports, and I think recent R versions assume methods as part of base; maybe cran has a separate policy though.

We have had endless headaches over the years every time we have tried to avoid putting methods into the Depends field. At a minimum, your package won't work if called via Rscript unless the --default-packages=methods argument is specified.

What is the preference of rstan devs about importing or depending on rstan? I chose to depend (not import) on rstan so that the rstan package is attached upon loading bDif, so all the rstan plotting and summary functions are also available. Is there a particular reason why I should choose to import instead of depend on stan (in the Description)?

CRAN has a stronger opinion that we do. The print and summary functions should work for a stanfit object even if rstan is only in the Imports field. If there are particular rstan functions you think your users will need, you can always import them and reexport them. For plotting, it is now better to use the bayesplot package directly (the rstanarm package does so now and rstan will follow).

Ben
